title: Laura Shimohara
text: Laura holds a bachelor’s degree in Biotechnology from the Federal University of Paraíba (2023) and is a PhD candidate. Her work focuses on bioinformatics and transcriptomics, with an emphasis on preprocessing long-read sequencing data and the in silico analysis of long non-coding RNAs.

title: João Cavalcante
text:
João holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Biomedicine and Bioinformatics from the Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte. He is a PhD student in Bioinformatics at BioME/IMD/UFRN.
His experience includes shotgun and 16S metagenomics; single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing; microarray analysis; differential gene expression; protein interaction networks; and biodiversity and functional analysis. He develops reproducible bioinformatics workflows using Nextflow and Snakemake and is interested in systems biology, metagenomics, network analysis, computational reproducibility, and open knowledge.

title: Diego Marques Coelho
text:
Diego holds a degree in Biological Sciences from the State University of Rio de Janeiro (2013), a master’s degree in Biological Sciences (Biophysics) from the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (2016), and a PhD in Bioinformatics from the Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte.
His recent academic work has used single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk RNA sequencing to investigate developmental neurobiology and the neuropathology of Alzheimer’s disease. He has worked as a bioinformatics analyst at Mendelics and as a bioinformatics developer at EMBL-EBI. He currently works at Ryvu Therapeutics and collaborates with researchers and biotechnology companies.

title: Marques-Coelho Bioinformatics Lab
text:
Welcome to the Marques-Coelho Bioinformatics Lab, a resource hub for our research, teaching, software, and scientific collaborations in molecular and computational biology.
Our work connects biological questions with reproducible data analysis. We develop and maintain workflows, analyze high-throughput sequencing data, and work with researchers to turn complex datasets into useful evidence.






Reproducible analysis and reporting for genomics, transcriptomics, metagenomics, and other omics projects.



Development and maintenance of portable pipelines with tools including Nextflow and Snakemake.



Research partnerships, training, and engagement with the wider bioinformatics community.





Meet our lab members and collaborators, or browse the lab’s scientific publications.

title: Gleison Medeiros
text:
Gleison is a master’s student in Bioinformatics at the Federal University of Rio Grande do Norte and holds a degree in Biomedicine from the same institution. His work focuses on omics data analysis, including single-cell data, RNA sequencing, metagenomics, and the evolution of biological systems.
Since 2021, he has been part of the BioME team, applying computational approaches to investigate evolutionary patterns and protein interaction networks.
